newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Ireland's Robinson, Chilean ex-leader share prize.
newsitem.headline: Ireland's Robinson, Chilean ex-leader share prize.

text.p: Irish President Mary Robinson and former Chilean president Patricio Aylwin were honoured on Friday for their work on behalf of human rights with the award of the North-South Lisbon Prize.

The annual award was being made in recognition of their "outstanding achievement regarding human rights protection, struggle for pluralist democracy and...solidarity," the Council of Europe's Lisbon-based North-South Centre said in a statement.
Aylwin was the first elected president of Chile on its return to democratic government in 1990 following 17 years of military rule.

"It is the people of Chile, true protagonists of this process (the return to democracy), who are being honoured through me. In their name, I thank you profoundly," Aylwin said in his acceptance speech.
Robinson has built up an international reputation as a firm defender of human rights during her seven years as Ireland's head of state.
A lawyer and noted orator, she is tipped as a future U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights after announcing she will not stand for re-election when her presidential term ends later this year.
Past winners of the North-South award include Danielle Mitterrand, widow of former French president Francois Mitterrand.
